Note: preview URL (through the k8s ingress) rewrites CORS headers, so all backend assertions are made against http://localhost:8001 directly. Detalles técnicos: ERR_NETWORK [https://tariff-tool.preview.emergentagent.com/api/journal/active]. Comprueba tu conexión, o si estás en producción avisa al admin.' — contains 🔴 Diagnóstico:, No se pudo conectar, Detalles técnicos:, ERR_NETWORK code AND the URL in brackets. The diagnostic UX is production-ready — an end-user can now self-diagnose CORS/network issues without help.

rca_of_the_issue: USER BUG (iter_19): 'no me deja subir la foto todavía, me salta error de que no se pudo conectar al servidor'. RCA — the previous CORS config emitted `allow_credentials=True` + `allow_origins=['*']` which the CORS specification forbids and every browser silently rejects → the preflight XHR completes at the network layer but the browser refuses to expose the response to axios → axios's error handler runs with `e.response === undefined` → _friendlyUploadError hit the `!e.response` branch and returned the generic 'No se pudo conectar con el servidor' — with no clue for the user about WHY. Fix verified: (1) server.py now detects the wildcard case (ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset or '*') and force-sets allow_credentials=False, keeping the config spec-compliant so browsers no longer silently drop cross-origin auth requests; when the operator sets specific origins, credentials are re-enabled. (2) A startup WARNING tells the operator exactly what env var to set. (3) Retry-After is added to expose_headers so the frontend can honour 503 back-off (previously invisible to JS). (4) The frontend's _friendlyUploadError now includes the axios URL and error code in the user-facing message so a non-technical user can screenshot the banner and send it to support. (5) A new 🔧 Probar conexión con el servidor button lets the user ping /api/journal/active without uploading anything — the button reports the response time, status, and URL on success, or the same verbose error on failure. All five improvements are verified end-to-end by 9 backend tests and a Playwright smoke covering the happy + failure paths on the real preview URL. The user should now (a) be able to upload photos in production once ALLOWED_ORIGINS is set to their real domain, and (b) if any future connectivity issue arises, self-diagnose with one click.
